about.title: San Juan Capistrano Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision is disorienting, especially in a close-knit city like San Juan Capistrano, where two people died in traffic crashes in the most recent reported year alongside 141 injury collisions. Grief doesn't leave much room for paperwork, insurance calls, or figuring out who has legal standing to bring a claim. That's where LawProactive comes in. We're not a law firm — we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent personal injury attorney experienced in wrongful death matters arising from crashes on corridors like Ortega Highway, Del Obispo Street, and the I-5. An attorney in our network can walk you through California's rules on who may file, what losses may be recoverable, and how much time you have to act. There's no fee unless there's a recovery, so you can focus on your family while someone else looks at the legal side.

whyChoose.title: Why San Juan Capistrano Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Explained Clearly
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to certain dependents or heirs if none exist. An attorney in our network can help clarify where your family fits.

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter window. Understanding this early matters, especially for crashes on state routes like the I-5.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help explain how these categories might apply to your situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of these survive the deceased, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. An independent attorney can review your family's specific circumstances to explain where you stand.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in San Juan Capistrano?
items.answer: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, may be involved — for example, in a crash on Ortega Highway — the deadline to act can be much shorter. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may arise from the same crash. The outcome of a criminal proceeding doesn't determine the outcome of a civil wrongful death claim, and families can pursue one whether or not criminal charges are filed.

items.question: What kinds of losses might our family be able to recover?
items.answer: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of that person's love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, so an attorney can help identify what applies to your case.
